prediction.likelyOutcome: Caton has a plausible but genuinely contested claim; the amendment recitals materially strengthen his reading of Section 9(a), but the Trust's condition-precedent argument is a real risk that could defeat the claim outright, and the undocumented expense proof will likely cause even a favorable verdict to trim the out-of-pocket component. Net expected value favors Caton but well below his full $442,885.50 demand, with meaningful odds of an unfavorable summary judgment ruling or trial loss on the liability gate.

issues.label: Factual Dispute Over Status of Adverse Possession Litigation at Termination

outcome.description: The circuit court granted Caton summary judgment on a futility theory and awarded him $442,885.50 in damages (the full amount of his demand) plus $96,329.00 in attorneys' fees. The Court of Appeals of Virginia affirmed that the agreement required Caton to exercise the option, but reversed the summary judgment award of damages and fees because futility was not established as a matter of law, and remanded for further proceedings.
outcome.finalNote: Summary judgment reversed and remanded; no final figure yet.
